source.title: When Does Learning Renormalize? Sufficient Conditions for Power Law Spectral Dynamics

record.file_problem: No apparent garbling, cutoff, or wrong-document issue; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses power-law learning dynamics and presents theory and measurements of GRSD spectral couplings, but it does not test or use any of the listed loss-scaling, compute-allocation, architecture-loss, or downstream-predictability versions.
record.gate_note: The empirical experiments measure spectral coupling structure for CIFAR-10 classifiers, not held-out loss as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute, or any other outcome named by V1–V7. Those spectral-structure results are recorded under fits_no_version. Cited scaling-law results are not recorded as study results.
record.test_reason: The study is a theory paper. Its experiments measure spectral coupling structure (diagonal Ωii vs λi, Toeplitz residuals) of the Jacobian-induced operator in CIFAR-10 ResNet-18 and PlainNet-18 at a single checkpoint. It reports no held-out loss against parameters, tokens or compute, and no extrapolation, compute-optimal split, architecture-loss comparison at scale, or downstream scaling. The power laws it derives are in a spectral velocity field, not in loss versus scale. The record's T6/discusses classification is correct.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors derive sufficient but not necessary conditions under which GRSD shell dynamics takes a power-law form. They argue that residual architectures approximately satisfy the key log-shift-invariance condition, with supporting spectral measurements on CIFAR-10. They explicitly deny that power-law scaling is universal.
record.recipe_differences: This is a theoretical GRSD study with spectral-coupling diagnostics on CIFAR-10 classifiers, not a reproduction of the original language-model loss-scaling measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The Toeplitz diagnostic changes with spectral-window position: ResNet-18 improves toward the intermediate spectral regime, while Toeplitz structure deteriorates near the spectral edges for both architectures.

fits_no_version.finding: On CIFAR-10 at a fixed checkpoint, ResNet-18's diagonal spectral couplings scale with eigenvalue with slope near 1 (R²≈0.99). Its shell coupling matrix becomes more Toeplitz toward the intermediate spectrum. PlainNet-18 shows more scatter and a flatter, weaker Toeplitz profile. Both degrade near the spectral edges.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Residual connections promote scale-free, log-shift-invariant spectral coupling of the training operator, a proposed mechanism for power-law learning dynamics. This is not a measurement of loss scaling.

record.problems: The evidence bearing on the broader scaling-law discussion is indirect: the experiments measure spectral couplings rather than held-out loss or downstream performance. Empirical evaluation is limited to ResNet-18 and PlainNet-18 on CIFAR-10 at a fixed checkpoint; the text gives no numerical PlainNet-18 fit values or Toeplitz residual values and reports no uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: No reported result on V1–V7 was omitted. The measured spectral-coupling outcomes are retained as rows with versions ["none"].

untested.parts: Held-out LM pretraining loss vs parameters, tokens and compute; not measured.
Extrapolation from small to large runs; not measured.
Loss vs depth, width or shape at fixed parameter count. The ResNet/PlainNet comparison is of spectral structure, not loss.
Power-law loss in other modalities or regimes. CIFAR-10 is used, but no loss-scaling curve is measured.
Downstream performance vs scale or loss; not measured.
Dependence of exponents or allocation on fitting and setup choices. The paper only argues theoretically that scaling can break when its conditions fail.

record.verdict_notes: All six rows correctly carry versions ['none'] and state cannot_determine. Cited scaling-law results (Kaplan, Hoffmann, Sorscher, etc.) are background only. The experiments involve no variation in model size, data or compute, and report no PlainNet numeric fits or uncertainty.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out language-model pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens, and compute.
Whether fits on small language-model runs predict much larger runs.
Compute-optimal parameter and token allocation, including how either changes with compute.
Loss effects of depth, width, and other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
Power-law loss behavior in other modalities or training regimes.
Downstream task performance as a function of scale or pretraining loss.
Dependence of published loss-scaling exponents or compute-optimal allocation on fitting and training choices, and departures of loss curves from a single power law.
